newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese inflation slowed in Aug - PM Guterres.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese inflation slowed in Aug - PM Guterres.

text.p: Portugal's benchmark inflation rate, the 12-month moving average, eased to 3.3 percent year-on-year in August from 3.4 percent in July, Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Wednesday night in New York.
The figure, which is in line with analysts' forecasts, was given at a meeting with bankers, the Diario Economico reported.
Guterres reaffirmed his confidence that the average rate would ease to three percent by the end of the year.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) is due to release August data by the end of the week. Analysts are expecting a month-on-month rise of between 0.1 and 0.3 percent, compared with 0.2 percent in July.
The monthly rate would give a year-on-year level of 3.4-3.6 percent, against 3.8 percent in July. The 12-month average would ease to 3.3 percent on any of these outcomes.

Guterres also repeated the government's optimism that the budget deficit will be around four percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, down from the official goal of 4.2 percent and 1995's 5.2 percent.
He said revenues from privatisations this year could rise to 450 billion escudos ($2.91 billion) from the 380 billion target the government had set.
